**Note first:** log covers `2026-07-04T02:00`–`02:31` UTC — ~7 weeks old, not last night. Either wrong file, or log rotation/shipping broken. Confirm before acting.

## What happened

Redis died, cache fell away, store got hammered, memory exploded, supervisor killed everything. ~17.5 min, single cause.

**Timeline**
| Time (UTC) | Event |
|---|---|
| 02:00–02:14 | Healthy. All 200s, cache hit ratio 0.90–0.98 |
| 02:14:07 | `ERROR [api] redis connection lost: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.0.0.12:6379` |
| 02:14:07 | `WARN [api] cache layer degraded — falling back to direct store reads` |
| 02:14:03 | last successful request logged — **no 200 after this point** |
| 02:14:10 | first `TimeoutError: request timed out after 5000ms (store overloaded)` |
| 02:15:26–02:31:26 | 13 reconnect attempts, all ECONNREFUSED, same IP |
| 02:29:12 | queue depth 502 crosses `max 500` |
| 02:31:44 | `ERROR [worker-2] JavaScript heap out of memory (request backlog)` |
| 02:31:45 | `FATAL [supervisor] worker-2 exited with code 134, restarting` |
| 02:31:52 | `FATAL [supervisor] api unresponsive, killing process group — service down` |

**Counts:** 174 cache-miss-storm WARN, 173 TimeoutError, 173 queue-depth WARN, 13 reconnect failures, 1 OOM, 2 FATAL.

## Root cause
Redis at `10.0.0.12:6379` refused connections at 02:14:07 and never came back. Everything after is downstream. Fallback to direct store reads made things worse: 100% miss traffic hit backing store, 5s timeouts, requests piled up in queue instead of shedding, queue backlog ate heap, worker-2 OOM (code 134 = SIGABRT), api unresponsive, supervisor killed process group.

Note: cache miss keys ran `orders:1000`→`orders:1119` monotonically — no repeats. Cache stampede on unique keys, not one hot key.

## Real problems exposed
1. **No load shedding.** Queue kept accepting past `max 500` — cap not enforced, only logged. This is what turned a cache outage into a total outage.
2. **Fallback has no circuit breaker.** Store timing out at 5000ms every request, still got retried. Should trip and fail fast.
3. **Reconnect has no backoff.** Attempts fixed ~80s apart, 13 tries, no growth, no give-up path or alert escalation.
4. **Timeout 5000ms too long** for a fallback path — 5s per stuck request × unbounded queue = heap death.

## Next
Check why Redis went down at 02:14:07 — nothing in this log explains it. Need Redis-side logs / infra events for that window. Also fix the log freshness issue first, else you're blind.
